name: Cinderwight
body:
Cinderwight
CR 15

This immense bird skeleton is covered in gray flame and rotting flesh. A poisonous cloud spreads beneath its wings and it seems to drain its surroundings of life.

XP 51,200
CE Gargantuan undead
Init +11; Senses darkvision 120 ft., detect magic, low-light vision, see invisibility; Perception +35
Aura deathshroud (20 ft., cloudkill, DC 26)

DEFENSE

AC 28, touch 14, flat-footed 20 (+7 Dex, +1 dodge, +14 natural, –4 size)
hp 210 (20d8+120); regeneration 10 (false immortality)
Fort +12, Ref +13, Will +16
Defensive Abilities channel resistance +4, false immortality; DR 15/good; Immune cold, fire, undead traits; SR 26

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 90 ft. (average)
Melee 2 talons +20 (2d6+8/19–20 plus energy drain) and bite +19 (2d8+8 plus energy drain)
Special Attacks energy drain (1 level, DC 26)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft.
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 18th)

Constant—detect magic, see invisibility
At will— bestow curse (DC 20), darkness, excruciating deformation (DC 19), greater contagion (DC 22), greater dispel magic, inflict critical wounds (DC 20)
3/day—quickened greater contagion (DC 22), harm (DC 22), horrid wilting (DC 24), mass inflict critical wounds (DC 24), slough (DC 21)

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 25, Con —, Int 13, Wis 18, Cha 22
Base Atk +15; CMB +27; CMD 45
Feats Combat Reflexes, Critical Focus, Dodge, Flyby Attack, Improved Critical (talon), Improved Initiative, Mobility, Quicken Spell-Like Ability (greater contagion), Staggering Critical, Weapon Focus (talon)
Skills Acrobatics +27, Fly +24, Intimidate +29, Perception +35, Sense Motive +27; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

False Immortality (Ex)

A cinderwight’s regeneration cannot be overcome with damage. To truly defeat a cinderwight, one has to cast resurrection or true resurrection on a cinderwight that’s below 0 hp. This resurrects the phoenix, destroying the cinderwight in the process.

Deathshroud (Su)

A cinderwight can cause its feathers to burst into unholy, warmthless fire as a free action. As long as its feathers are burning, it inflicts energy drain with each natural attack, and any creature within reach (20 feet for most cinderwights) must make a DC 26 Fortitude save each round to avoid being afflicted as if it failed a save against the cloudkill spell. A creature that attacks the cinderwight with natural or non-reach melee weapons takes 1d6 points of negative energy damage (no save) with each successful hit. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Cinderwights are unholy creatures that come into being from the remains of a noble phoenix in very specific circumstances. Normally these majestic beasts cannot resurrect on desecrated ground, but that fact can unfortunately be bypassed. If slain by energy drain and then subjected to the desecrate spell right as they self-resurrect (for example by the spell being readied), the process goes awry and they corrupt into creatures known as cinderwights. Physically, these undead share much with their previous form, including size and tenacity, if not beauty. Mentally, their faculties are damaged, and their typically noble and good disposition suffers a complete turnaround. Cinderwights spread plague, poison and death instead of health and succor. Their monstrous magic brings disease and deformity and the gray flame that covers their rotting bodies poisons and damages the hardiest creatures, even killing the lesser beings outright. Cinderwights are incredibly hard to create, requiring one to locate and neutralize the phoenix, kill it in a specific way and time the desecration with incredible precision. Any evil force that manages to do so is greeted by death on wings that not only can depopulate whole regions in mere days, but cannot be slain itself unless resurrected back into the phoenix form, which the creature itself vehemently defends itself against. The enterprising necromancers and other beings that try to create these undead monstrosities should exercise caution, as newly created cinderwights not only feel no compulsion to serve the tormentors of their souls, but very eagerly attack and tear them apart as first victims.

Cinderwights attack relentlessly, knowing they cannot be truly destroyed by the unprepared. They prefer attacking large population centers, sowing as much death and disease as possible with their aura and spell-like abilities. Whether assaulting a city or facing opposition, they target divine casters first, both out of self-preservation and of pure spite for the forces they once eagerly championed. Rarely, an evil phoenix may be bent enough on destruction with no regard for self?preservation that it decides to set the whole process up and turn itself into a deathless horror. Such cinderwights sometimes retain some or all of their original personality, though their intelligence and wisdom scores are almost always lower than in their original form, as the transformation into the very antithesis of a phoenix strains their minds greatly even if done of own volition. Cinderwights, being undead forms of phoenixes, are of equal size to their living form, but weigh only half as much due to most of their flesh rapidly rotting off. This bluish, misty outline of a man is blurred and vague, though undoubtedly presents a decrepit figure contorted in fear and rage.
